content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 19.2, ¶p0076).**

The warranty package is mostly acceptable — §19.1 gives professional/workmanlike services plus documentation conformance, §19.3 covers malicious code and legal compliance, §19.4 provides re-performance/repair/replacement with a refund backstop and expressly non-exclusive treatment for fraud/IP/security claims, and §19.5's disclaimer expressly does not limit express warranties or remedies.

The single failure point is duration: §19.2 caps Deliverable conformance at **fifteen days** and then declares Vendor has *no correction or refund obligation* thereafter — which not only falls below our fallback (90/30) but also switches off the §19.4 remedy and hollows out the otherwise unlimited §19.1 warranty.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) extends the period to twelve months for Deliverables and delivered software and ninety days for Services, deletes the sunset sentence, and confirms the §19.4 remedies remain available and non-exclusive — with the 90/30 fallback flagged in the comment.
